title: What if all delivery companies could use the same network?
summary: Read What if all delivery companies could use the same network? and explore insights on autonomous delivery, innovation, and Arrive AI updates.
body_markdown:
Think about how many different companies deliver packages today.


You might receive an order from Amazon, have medication delivered by a pharmacy, or use another company when you need to send something back.


Each company has its own delivery process. But what if they could all use the same network?


That's the idea behind what we're building at Arrive AI.


We're working toward a delivery network that can support different companies and delivery methods, including drones, robots, and traditional delivery drivers.


We're also exploring how this network can make everyday tasks easier, from receiving packages to returning items.


# Bringing drone delivery to pharmacies


One of the ways we're putting this idea into practice is through our newly announced pharmacy delivery program with Lifespan and CarDon in the greater Indianapolis area.


The network includes around 20 pharmacy and nursing home locations.


The program explores how drones can help deliver medications between healthcare locations. But delivering medication requires more care than delivering an ordinary package.


Some medications need to stay within certain temperature ranges. It's also important to know who handled them and when they were received.


Concept illustration of a drone lowering a pharmacy package into an Arrive Point™ outside a hospital.


That's why the program includes important features such as:


- Delivery records: Keeping track of how medications are handled during delivery.
- Temperature control: Heated and cooled cargo areas for items that need special temperature conditions.
- Secure delivery: Providing a safe place for medications to arrive and be received.


These are important parts of making pharmacy deliveries more reliable.


# Why should different delivery companies use the same network?


Imagine having a different delivery box for every company that brings packages to your home.


One company uses its own box. Another needs a separate system. And another has a completely different setup.


That would make receiving packages more complicated.


Arrive AI is working toward a different approach: one delivery network that different companies can use.


Think about electric vehicle charging. Drivers don't necessarily need a different charging station for every car brand. Shared charging networks allow different vehicles to use the same locations.


We see a similar opportunity with package delivery.


Instead of every delivery company building its own network of delivery boxes, different providers could use the same receiving locations.


This could make package delivery easier for homes, businesses, pharmacies, and other locations.


# Making different delivery methods work together


Not every package will be delivered the same way.


Some may arrive by drone. Others may be delivered by robots, self-driving vehicles, or traditional delivery drivers.


As these options continue to grow, they will need places where packages can be safely received.


Our goal is to make the Arrive Point Network work with different delivery companies and delivery methods.


This means a delivery provider would not have to depend on a completely separate receiving system just to deliver a package.


We want to make it easier for different companies to use the same network.


# What about package returns?


Receiving packages is one part of online shopping. Returning them is another.


Think about the last time you needed to return something you bought online.


You may have had to find the order, look for the return instructions, print a label, and drive to a shipping store.


Now imagine being able to start that process from the same place where you receive your packages.


That's another part of what we're working toward at Arrive AI.


The Arrive Point Network is designed to support package returns, too.


Through the Arrive AI app, the goal is to let users view their recent purchases, choose an item they want to return, and start the return process.


From there, the system is designed to help arrange a pickup through a shipping company based on the return details.


The idea is to make returning online orders easier without having to visit different shipping stores or drop-off locations.


# Keeping track of your packages in one place


Another common problem with online shopping is keeping track of everything you order.


You might buy something from one store, order groceries from another, and receive packages from several delivery companies.


Sometimes it's hard to remember what you ordered or which company is handling the delivery.


Arrive AI is working toward an app that brings package information together in one place.


The goal is to let users check their deliveries, see package updates, and manage returns without having to search through different websites and services.


Instead of checking several places, you could have one place to manage your deliveries.


# One network for sending, receiving, and returning packages


Package delivery is changing. Drones and robots are creating new ways to move items, while traditional delivery companies continue to serve homes and businesses.


But no matter how a package travels, it still needs a place to arrive.


At Arrive AI, we're working toward one shared network that can support different delivery companies and make sending, receiving, and returning packages easier.


Our pharmacy delivery program with Lifespan and CarDon is one example of how this network could support different needs.


And as we continue developing the Arrive Point Network, our goal remains the same: make package delivery simpler and more convenient for everyone.


Because people shouldn't need a different system for every company that delivers to their door.
